data.title: Micron appoints industry veteran Hanford to lead its research institution
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) appointed tech sector veteran Deirdre Hanford to serve as president of Micron Research Labs, the memory maker's long-horizon research institution, which was announced last month and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho. 

The global research institution is backed by a $10B investment from Micron over the next 10 years. Its research will include critical memory process technologies, future memory and compute architectures, advanced packaging and next-generation semiconductor manufacturing.

"Micron Research Labs was created to pursue the breakthroughs that will define the future of memory, compute and AI, and Deirdre is uniquely qualified to lead that mission," said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer of Micron Technology. "She combines deep semiconductor industry expertise with a proven ability to build partnerships, inspire collaboration and turn ambitious ideas into lasting impact."

Hanford spent nearly 40 years at Synopsys (SNPS). Her roles included chief security officer, co-general manager of the Design Group and executive vice president of customer engagement. She currently serves on the UC Berkeley College of Engineering Advisory Board, the MIT School of Engineering Dean's Advisory Council and the SEMI Board of Industry Leaders.

data.title: FTAI Aviation announces $500M buyback plan; shares in focus
data.description:
• FTAI Aviation (FTAI) authorized a new $500M share repurchase program to buy back its outstanding ordinary shares.
  • The company plans to use cash on its balance sheet to fund the buybacks.
  • The program will run through September 30, 2029, unless completed earlier.
  • The shares may be repurchased through the open market or private transactions, depending on market conditions.
  • The program does not require the company to repurchase any specific amount, and the timing and size of purchases will depend on its share price and market conditions.
  • On the market side, the FTAI stock traded nearly 4% higher at ~$182.99 in the after-hours trading session.
  • Source: Press Release

data.description:

  • Torq plans to use the net proceeds for general working capital.

data.title: 3M, DuPont face Connecticut firefighters’ PFAS lawsuit
data.description:
A U.S. federal judge has allowed Connecticut firefighters to pursue claims against more than 20 companies, including 3M (MMM) and DuPont (DD), alleging that chemicals in protective gear exposed them to toxic "forever chemicals" and increased their cancer risk.

U.S. District Judge Alvin Thompson in Hartford, Connecticut, ruled Tuesday that 13 firefighter unions and 12 individual firefighters had sufficient grounds to seek damages and medical monitoring, even when they had no outward symptoms of cancer or other diseases.

The plaintiffs allege that PFAS in protective "turnout gear" can enter the body through skin absorption, ingestion, and inhalation. Their lawyers have described the case as the first proposed class action focused exclusively on firefighter equipment containing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or PFAS.

Thompson also found that the plaintiffs had adequately alleged that 3M (MMM) had a duty to warn about the risks associated with the chemicals and had acted negligently.

According to the complaint, 3M’s (MMM) Scotchlite reflective material and DuPont’s (DD) Kevlar were among the PFAS-containing components used in firefighters’ protective gear, while Honeywell (HON) manufactured the turnout gear. Some liabilities associated with DuPont (DD) now belong to spinoffs Chemours (CC) and Corteva (CTVA).

The companies have sought to have the claims dismissed. 3M (MMM) argued there were no plausible allegations connecting Scotchlite to the firefighters’ gear, while other defendants disputed claims that the equipment failed to protect firefighters from fire-related hazards.

The lawsuit was filed in June 2024.

data.title: Sabre prices $1.35B senior notes at 9.875% to refinance debt
data.description:
• Sabre (SABR) announced on Tuesday that it priced an upsized $1.35B offering of 9.875% senior secured notes due 2032, up from the previously planned $1.1B.
  • The offering is expected to close on September 28.
  • The notes will pay 9.875% annual interest, in semiannual payments, and mature on October 15, 2032.
  • The net proceeds will be used to refinance existing borrowings, including Sabre’s 11.125% senior secured notes due 2029.
  • The company also plans to repay an existing intercompany loan as part of the transaction.
  • Separately, Sabre GLBL plans to launch tender offers for up to $250M of certain existing senior secured notes.
  • Overall, the transactions are aimed at replacing higher-cost and existing debt with the new financing and managing Sabre’s debt maturities.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: SA analyst: Rising rates could trigger major market volatility
data.description:
Wall Street declined Tuesday as investors positioned ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision Wednesday, with elevated borrowing costs and geopolitical risks keeping pressure on markets.

Seeking Alpha analyst Andrew Hecht warned that the central bank’s September meeting could prove particularly consequential as inflation remains elevated and the U.S. midterm elections approach.

“Market consensus is for a 25-basis-point rate hike,” Hecht stated, adding that the ongoing and spreading conflict in the Middle East is “driving inflation higher.”

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) in the session fell -0.6%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) declined -0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) lost -0.7%.

Hecht said the September meeting may be the Federal Reserve’s final opportunity to raise rates before the midterms without facing accusations of political favoritism. “The real surprise tomorrow would be no change,” he said.

Meanwhile, long-term Treasury futures have fallen below October 2023 technical support, reaching their lowest level since July 2007, according to Hecht.

He attributed rising rates partly to the nation’s more than $40 trillion debt burden, calling higher borrowing costs a “danger sign” for markets across asset classes.

Hecht urged investors to remain cautious, citing seasonal volatility, economic and geopolitical uncertainty, and the approaching midterm elections as potential catalysts for larger market swings.
